steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Brr, it's cold.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: All the more reason to knock, instead of wasting time out here.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: But I don't know her that well.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Glad to see you're as shy as ever, even after all these years.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: It still feels weird that we've become colleagues, even after all these years.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Alright, then I guess I'll help you out, as a colleague.

steps.name: Leithanian Woman
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Miss Bachmann, this is Glacier, the 'Earthspirit' whom you wrote to.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Ah, yes. I found a box labeled 'To Glacier' written on it while going through my late mother's belongings, so I asked you to come and pick it up.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: And you're finally here.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I was on my way to visit family, so I stopped by to see what Professor Bachmann had for me.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Please, come in.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: We pried the box open because we didn't know what was in it. Only after reading the letter inside did we learn it was meant for you.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: We're still not sure what the stuff we found is, though. I wonder if you could tell us.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Hm... a piece of paper and a rock?

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: We came all this way for this?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: It's a design for an Arts Unit inhibitor, but still very much in the theoretical stage.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: She taught me how to hear the vibrations of certain minerals using Originium Arts, but all that turned to pure noise after I became Infected.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: At least treatment at Rhodes Island put an end to that. Now I can hear them again, even clearer than before.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: At the time, though, we were at our wits' end. She believed the Oripathy increased my Arts output, so she said she'd make me an inhibitor after I'd worked for a full year.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: An Arts Unit?

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: How hard can it be to order a custom-made Arts Unit in Leithanien? Why did Mom have to do it herself?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Simply suppressing my Arts would have prevented me from hearing the sounds at all.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: So it could only be made by someone familiar with both the Arts involved and the vibration frequencies of minerals, who could manually calibrate the inhibition of different wavelengths—like tuning an instrument.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Sounds fascinating. Too bad she never completed it.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I could still use an inhibitor like that, though... If she'd come this far, perhaps I could continue her research.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: What about the rock then?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: It's a beacon stone.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Sorry, I'll need more of an explanation than that.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Some rocks undergo metamorphism when they come into contact with Originium, resulting in metamorphic rock that contains Originium.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Such rocks react to my Originium Arts, allowing me to sense them with the help of a tuning fork.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: The professor would use the rocks with the strongest reactions as beacon stones.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: We used to bring them on our field trips, leaving them behind to mark our path.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Wouldn't your beacon stones get mixed up with others using the same method to pass through the same area?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Not many people do this in the first place, and it's even less likely that their stones would use the same frequency. If anything, it would help us identify who else had passed through.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Sounds like a convenient Art.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: It's just about causing small vibrations in matter. Frequency control is a relatively minor part, the key is understanding the mineral composition.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: So why did she leave this to you?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Perhaps it's a clue, a way of asking me to use my Arts to search the city for this beacon's frequency.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Is that okay with you, Parker?

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Should be fine, as long as it doesn't endanger public safety, or draw the attention of others.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I sense a trail leading outside the city.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Should we check it out?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Now?

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: If not now, when? You're leaving tomorrow, aren't you?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I could always come back another time.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: And Professor Bachmann always told me that curiosity leads to ruin.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: This is a nomadic city, you know. You may not be able to pick up the trail next time, if it's outside the city.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I'm here on vacation, not for work.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: This isn't exactly work, is it? Whatever you find belongs to you. Walk a few steps, make some easy money.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: We have time, Earthspirit. I just heard from the hotel that it's going to be a couple of hours before they get the room ready anyway.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: They sure are sloppy...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Alright, we'll go and try to get this done before dark.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Never thought I'd see a place like this outside the city.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Are you sure it's here?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Yes, this is where the signal led.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Hm... a cave with a tunnel leading beyond. The entrance has caved in.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Huh? Is this mine what mom left you?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: It seems to have been abandoned long ago. And I'm not aware of her owning any private mines.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: The signal goes further in.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: It's beneath the cave-in.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Beneath? We should have brought tools.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Leave it to me.
Earthspirit touches the ground with the end of her staff, and the collapsed area begins to liquefy.
Then, the ground begin to roil.
Soon, an elaborate metal box rises to the surface.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: There must be something valuable inside!
That's good news.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Hey, what are you doing?

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Thanks for the heads-up. Now I can get my hands on the full legacy of Professor Bachmann.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Miss Bachmann?! Was this a trap?

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Sorry. I wish there was another way, but my husband insists that we tie up all loose ends.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: We can leave once we sell these, right honey? We can live a better life in Columbia, like you said?

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Ngh!

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Her leg? Where are you aiming? Shoot to kill, not maim.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: What are you doing? Are you out of your mind?!

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: You have no idea how much time and effort I spent planning this.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: But Bachmann left behind little beyond a house and a bunch of useless rocks.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: And now that I have my hands on the last remaining piece of the inheritance, I don't need you. I'd rather not have to split the spoils.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: This will give me the capital I need to make a comeback in the Columbian mining sector.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Just look at this. An abandoned mine outside the nomadic city. An opportunity of a lifetime.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Stop this!

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: My dear Miss Glacier, I hear you've turned down invitations from multiple Rim Billiton companies.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Join me, and I'll allow you to live and serve me. I'll even give you a leadership position.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Sorry, I'm not looking for a career change. The pay may be nothing to write home about, but working for Rhodes Island has many perks for an Infected.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Have you never thought about escaping the cage of everyday life?

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: About a vacation, where you don't have to worry about when you'll return to work.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: About having time to just lie in bed, without needing to think about anything.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Don't you want to live a life like that?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Who doesn't?

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Then join me. You'll have authority, and plenty of vacation time.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: You said the same thing to Miss Bachmann, didn't you?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I'll admit your words may be tempting to the young.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: But I've been around long enough to know that jobs like that simply don't exist. Anything offering such great conditions is probably a scam.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Still, sparing your life was part of that offer. You would be wise not to defy me.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: It's bothersome enough keeping track of my boss' condition at Rhodes Island. I took leave for New Year's, and I'd rather spend it on my own projects, thank you very much.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: It hurts... Ugh...

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Oh, shut up.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Kill her first!

steps.name: Mercenary A
steps.text: Want us to shoot her?

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: With your aim? No need to prolong her misery, just get it over with.

steps.name: Mercenary Captain
steps.text: Draw your swords!

steps.name: Mercenary A
steps.text: Hey, I can't move! Something's grabbing my feet!

steps.name: Mercenary B
steps.text: No, you're sinking!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: You shall not pass.

steps.name: Mercenary A
steps.text: Help! It's up to my chest! I can't breathe!

steps.name: Mercenary B
steps.text: Grab my hand!

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Damn it!

steps.name: Mercenary B
steps.text: We can't get through!

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Is this your final answer, Glacier?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Take it however you'd like.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: I changed my mind. Kill all three of them.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Wait, I haven't—

steps.name: Mercenary Captain
steps.text: Switch to crossbows. Shoot them from a distance!

steps.name: Mercenary B
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Mercenary Captain
steps.text: Target the Caprinae! Kill her and stop her Arts!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: You're not hurting my colleague.

steps.name: Mercenary Captain
steps.text: Oh, forgot about you.

steps.name: Mercenary A
steps.text: Captain, this place is too cramped. They could easily block all our bolts with that shield, and the Caprinae's Arts are preventing us from closing in.

steps.name: Mercenary Captain
steps.text: What a pain...

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: I'm not paying you to stand around! Do something!

steps.name: Mercenary Captain
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Mercenary Captain
steps.text: How about this? Explosive bolts we found at the cave entrance!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Not gonna happen!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: What? They're aiming above our heads?

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Cause of death: cave-in due to disrepair. What a perfect conclusion!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Watch out—
Miss Bachmann looks up and sees only a great mass of black.
A tire-sized rock falls towards her.
Before she has finished processing what is going on, a white hand enters her field of vision.
Rocks turn to sand when they touch it, and flow through the gaps in its fingers onto her cheeks, still warm from the hand's touch.
She sees a Caprinae grabbing her shoulder with one hand, the other hand raised high in the air.
She smells a familiar scent of dirt and grass, just like that of her mother.
A sense of security surrounds her, one that she had forgotten for close to twenty years.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Are you okay?

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Thank you... you could do that?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: It only took a few calculations.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Glad I wasn't late this time.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: They're aiming deeper!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: The whole place is coming down!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Are they trying to bury us alive?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Get over here, Parker!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: I think we should run!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: She can't walk! And those guys have blocked the way!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Well, we can't just sit here on our thumbs!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Just trust me!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Wait, Earthspirit!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Stop! The warning light on your monitoring ring has turned red!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: A false positive.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Are those... bones?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Don't look.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Stick close!

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Hahaha! Die!
At first, the rocks turn into sand of various colors, like stars falling from the sky.
The grains gradually increase in size, hitting the ground like the spring rain.
The rocks at a distance also begin to fall, hitting the ground hard.
Rather than swallowing the three of them up, the liquefied ground rises like the tide and lifts them.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Earthspirit?!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I'm fine, just calibrating things! Cover your nose and mouth, and don't let any dust get into your body, or you'll be making a lot of trips to the doctor!

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: You're analyzing the composition of each falling rock and each inch of earth, and vibrating them at different frequencies? And you call that 'a few calculations'?

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: If anything goes wrong...

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: W-What's going on?

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: She can't move right now! Shoot! Shoot her!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Oh no!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Not so fast.
The falling dust suddenly turns back into stone, blocking the incoming bolts as they fall.
As they hit the ground, they send forth ripples, as though falling into water, which build into waves that surge towards the cave entrance.
And as those waves come into contact with the people standing there, the liquefied earth returns to normal.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: I—I can't move!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Tie them up, Parker, and call the police.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Wait! Did you think she was innocent?

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Forging the will, stealing the inheritance—she was my accomplice from beginning to end.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: It was her idea to use you to find the final legacy!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Forging the will and stealing the inheritance?!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Why did you do that, Miss Bachmann?

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: You never realized? Mom never loved me. She only ever had eyes for my brother.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: I never got anything from her... so it's only fair that I get a bigger slice of the inheritance.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: What on Terra are you talking about?! Do you realize what you did? You were plotting with that guy to exploit me just minutes ago!

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Mom did so much for you, it's the least you could do to help me escape this hell!

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: I wasn't going to take your life...

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Look, I'm a recent graduate, and I've been all over the place looking for a job. But with this money, I wouldn't have to work at all; I could sleep-in all day if I wanted to.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: ...You're a spoiled brat.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: What do you know? You only visit home once a year. Adults like you only care about work, never about your family. You deserve to drown in the endless cycle of mundane life.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I'm not in a position to defend the image you have of Professor Bachmann.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: But you have no right to criticize me, or anyone who works hard and lives their lives seriously!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Yes, I'm a jerk who hardly ever goes home.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Besides my work at Rhodes Island, I also accept jobs as a Catastrophe Messenger to make some extra cash.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Do you know why?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Did you think I do it just so I don't have to go home? Do you think anyone LIKES living like that?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I was born and raised outside the nomadic cities, in a tiny town with nothing.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: That's what I consider home, and it never moves. It's not so bad when there's a nomadic city nearby, but they're never around forever, and they always leave us behind.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: What will my family do when a Catastrophe comes, if I don't make enough money for them to move to a nomadic city?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I may be a Catastrophe Messenger, but that doesn't mean I have a solution other than paying to get them out of harm's way.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Maybe you think you could live without a care, unlike the rest of us. But if you don't care about the deeper issue, then at least spare me your juvenile sense of superiority!

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: I worked for this inheritance!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Would you have gotten any of it without me? Even your Leonard here's been working harder than you.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: Actually, it's Louis—

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Shut up! I don't care what your name is!
The normally quiet Caprinae roars.
But the collapsed cave walls do not echo her voice.
Even the skulking skeletal creature behind her whimpers and backs off.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: ...Yes, ma'am.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: ...Huff...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: As far as I know, Miss Bachmann, your mother loved you.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: She worked four jobs—professor, geologist, Catastrophe Messenger, and pianist—because she loved you and wanted you to have a better life.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Your older brother suffered from malnutrition as a child, leading to all sorts of complications, and she was worried that you'd end up like him.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: She gave you a comfortable life, and the best education money can buy in Leithanien, but also your current... immaturity...

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: So what? You say she gave me all that, but was hardly ever home. She wasn't so busy that she couldn't take a single day off, was she?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: One time, she wanted to take some time off and spend it with you.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: But then I slipped and fell in a cave during some fieldwork.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: She said I was in bad shape, covered in cuts from the exposed Originium.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: She had to patch me up and drive me all the way to Rhodes Island. So... it was my fault.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: If she'd gone home back then, and you talked out your feelings together, then perhaps she'd have retired earlier, and things could have gone differently.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: This is my fault. My curiosity was the cause of all this.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Just like she taught me: curiosity leads to ruin.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: If you know it's your fault, then leave me alone, and let me live my life!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: But this man will throw you under the bus the moment I hand him over to the police. You want me to let him go too?

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: He's got a criminal record; I had to get someone smuggle him into the city. Destroy his fake documents, and they won't let him in.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: That's the best way to get rid of him.

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: You... you backstabbing bitch!

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: You betrayed me first!

steps.name: Louis
steps.text: You'd be dead already if I could move!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: So, are you asking me to make the decision?

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: You said you were sorry, right? Then let me live my life.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I'm sorry... Miss Bachmann.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Making decisions is for leaders. I just do the job I'm paid for.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Besides, you dragged me into your family matters while I'm on vacation. Can you pay me overtime?

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: What?! You dirty, stinking Infected...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I'll take you to the hospital to get your wounds treated, and then ask your brother what he thinks. If he's okay with it, things can stay as they are.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: If not, then it's off to the courts.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: You'll ruin my life!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Maybe you ruined it all on your own.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Let's split up, Parker. We'll meet up in front of the Bachmann home once we're done.

steps.name: Miss Bachmann
steps.text: Wait!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Everything's taken care of on my end.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Didn't think I'd ever see you lose control like that.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Ahem. I never lost control...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: It was just... let's call it stress relief.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: What are you looking at?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Their house. The last time I was here, the plants in the garden were trimmed, and the walls were neat and clean. How did it get so run down in just a few years?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Professor Bachmann worked so hard to support her family, and for what?

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: I guess you should spend more time with them when you're the head of the household.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Now explain the monitoring ring, Earthspirit. Under normal circumstances, I'd be required to report that to the HQ immediately.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Did you see that thing behind me?

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Just a faint silhouette. Was it a living thing?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Yes. Not everyone can see it, but it gets clearer when I cast Originium Arts. It should've been fairly visible back there.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: My Arts depend on accurate control of the output. Most vibrations only require a small amount of energy, and the rest goes to waste.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: And since only a little bit of it is used, the excess gets radiated.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: At some point it began to draw in creatures like that, which feed on the waste energy.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: And with the help of the Casters at Rhodes Island, I discovered how to draw upon the energy contained inside it.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: But that causes a direct flowback into my body.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Which is why the warning light on the monitoring ring lit up.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: So there's no need to worry, but we'll need to do something about the data. I don't want to be put on medical leave if the Doctor or Kal'tsit finds out.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: You've never been a good liar, so I'll believe you.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Thanks, Parker.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Oh? Sounds like you had quite the adventure over your vacation.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Too much adventure for me, I'm afraid. I took a detour to see Professor Bachmann's daughter, but I never imagined the trouble that'd bring me.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Don't eat so much fried food. Here, have some veggies.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: But a little bit now and then improves my mood. Want some fries?

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: I guess that means your mood needs improving?

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Don't push yourself too hard, okay? But no, I don't even know how you can stomach those cold, soggy things.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: So, what was in the box?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Geological units collected from north of Ursus.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Sounds like things are about to get busy for you.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Not really. The professor said these came from unexplored lands. We may not get a chance to visit there in our lifetimes.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: She always said she'd leave them to me someday, but I didn't expect her to already have made the preparations.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Isn't it hard for researchers like you to keep your curiosity in check?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I still have a lot of hobbies. I get to do what I like after work, rather than worrying about what needs my attention.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Besides, I made a promise to the professor.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: My job is just to keep these safe, and report to Kal'tsit and the Doctor. Nothing more, nothing less.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: ...I just remembered that I still haven't made my report.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Ugh... looks like another rough afternoon.
